evidence_items.locator: Section 3, application A1; figure 4(a); appendix D, A1
evidence_items.explanation: On the matched 120-problem subset, figure 4(a) reports 48.33% success for ChatGPT with Code Interpreter, 45.0% with Wolfram Alpha, and 30.0% for vanilla GPT-4. These are substantial practical gains for both plug-ins, although the comparison does not fully isolate differences between the web products and baseline configuration.

evidence_items.publisher: Tanuj Kumar and Mikhail A. Kats, arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Executive summary; section 3, problem-solving performance table

receipt.public_excerpt: accurate symbolic manipulations and numerical calculations.

evidence_items.explanation: Repeated trials on the same 13 math and electromagnetism problems show clear gains: the line-charge problem improves from 0/10 correct to 6/10, and the two-charge force problem from 1/10 to 10/10. These are individual-trial results, separate from the paper's additional consensus-answer procedure.

unresolved_gaps: The evaluations do not hold every hidden model and product setting constant.
They do not establish a universal improvement across all mathematics and science subjects.
The selected sources do not report exact experiment dates; the results were public before the post.
